note: Each entry carries its provenance: V verified at the primary page on the date checked; S located through search and read in the search result, not re-read in full; K from background knowledge, link not re-read this session; U unconfirmed or proposed. Obligation says how firmly an entry applies: Mandatory, Endorsed (by the Data Standards Authority or the Open Standards Board), Recommended, Voluntary, In review or Proposed. The DSA list was read on 20 November 2026; its GOV.UK catalogue page was last updated 25 October 2023, so statuses may lag.

sources.title: Open standards for government data and technology
Government Security: GovAssure and Secure by Design

standards.name: Essential Shared Data Assets (ESDA) policy
standards.purpose: Identify the data assets that are critical across government, give each an owner, assess its quality, make it findable and make it available through APIs.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK pages found by search on 20 November 2026: the ESDA policy (updated 26 April 2024) and 'Make essential shared data assets available across government', which says all ESDAs must be assessed for data quality issues, made findable and be available through APIs. Status on the policy page: rolled out to beta, then to be reviewed.

standards.name: Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files (RFC 4180)
standards.purpose: The common format for publishing tabular data as CSV.
standards.evidence: Read at the DSA Standards Catalogue page (published 28 July 2023, updated 25 October 2023) on 8 November 2026: listed as Endorsed, entry updated 2 February 2021; the catalogue gives no licence.

standards.name: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT)
standards.purpose: W3C vocabulary for describing datasets and data services in catalogues; the base vocabulary xGov MEM builds on.
standards.evidence: xGov MEM classes map to dcat:Dataset, dcat:DataService and dcat:Distribution (read from the vendored model). GOV.UK guidance "Using metadata to describe data assets in a data catalogue" (updated 28 September 2023) says to use DCAT version 3, endorsed by the DSA for connecting departmental catalogues to the Government Data Catalogue (search-sourced, 20 November 2026).

standards.name: Open Document Format (ODF) 1.2
standards.purpose: Open formats for documents, spreadsheets and presentations, so they can be opened without one supplier's software.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: ODF 1.2, Endorsed, updated 2021-02-02. GOV.UK's open standards page also says PDFs on GOV.UK must become HTML or have an HTML or OpenDocument version (search-sourced).

standards.name: Open Referral UK
standards.publisher: Open Referral UK (endorsed by the DSA)
standards.purpose: Describe local services (who provides what, where and when) so directories can share the information.
standards.evidence: Read at the DSA Standards Catalogue page (published 28 July 2023, updated 25 October 2023) on 8 November 2026: listed as Endorsed, CC BY-SA 4.0, entry updated 16 March 2021.

standards.name: UK Cross-Government Metadata Exchange Model (xGov MEM)
standards.purpose: A common model for describing datasets, data services and distributions so catalogues across government can exchange metadata.
standards.status: Endorsed for implementation by the Data Standards Authority Steering Board
standards.evidence: Model content verified: vendored from co-cddo/ukgov-metadata-exchange-model at commit d6d9a24. Endorsement wording is from the published model page as recorded by the owner; page not re-read this session. Not listed in the DSA Standards Catalogue page as read on 8 November 2026.

standards.name: UK GEMINI
standards.purpose: The UK's metadata standard for describing geospatial datasets and services.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: UK Gemini, Endorsed, updated 2020-12-01, tags Semantics and Metadata. Link from background knowledge.

standards.name: Tabular data standard
standards.purpose: How to structure tables of data for sharing and publishing so machines and people read them the same way.
standards.evidence: Listed on the GOV.UK "Recommended open standards for government" page (last updated 28 September 2023), read on 20 November 2026; title only.

standards.name: UK Geospatial Data Standards Register
standards.purpose: The standards to use when publishing geospatial data, in line with DSA recommendations.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK publication found by search on 20 November 2026: says these standards should be used for publishing geospatial data in line with the National Data Strategy and DSA recommendations.

standards.name: Using metadata to describe CSV data (CSV on the Web)
standards.purpose: Describe a CSV file's columns, types and meaning in a companion metadata file so others can use it without guessing.
standards.evidence: Listed on the GOV.UK "Recommended open standards for government" page (last updated 28 September 2023), read on 20 November 2026; title only, the guidance itself not re-read.

standards.name: Using metadata to describe data shared within government
standards.purpose: The minimum metadata to record when data is shared between government organisations.
standards.evidence: Listed on the GOV.UK "Recommended open standards for government" page (last updated 28 September 2023), read on 20 November 2026; title only.

standards.name: Using metadata to describe tabular data for publishing
standards.purpose: The metadata to publish alongside tables of data.
standards.evidence: Listed on the GOV.UK "Recommended open standards for government" page (last updated 28 September 2023), read on 20 November 2026; title only.

standards.name: DCAT-AP-UK (proposed UK application profile of DCAT)
standards.publisher: Independent proposal by the owner of this server
standards.purpose: A proposed UK profile of DCAT that also describes APIs as data services. Proposed to supersede xGov MEM; not endorsed by any government body.
standards.evidence: Proposal recorded by the owner (open item O-18). Not in the DSA list read on 20 November 2026.

standards.name: API technical and data standards
standards.purpose: How government APIs should be built and described: RESTful design, JSON, OpenAPI documentation, secure transport and versioning.
standards.evidence: Named in GOV.UK's 'Government technology standards and guidance' list and on the DSA group page (search-sourced, 20 November 2026). The guidance page itself could not be opened this session; link and summary from background knowledge.

standards.name: OpenAPI 3 (describing RESTful APIs)
standards.purpose: A machine-readable way to describe RESTful APIs.
standards.evidence: Read at the GOV.UK recommended open standards page (updated 28 September 2023) on 8 November 2026. Not in the DSA Standards Catalogue.

standards.name: Unique Property Reference Number (UPRN) and Unique Street Reference Number (USRN)
standards.publisher: Open Standards Board (GeoPlace maintains the identifiers)
standards.purpose: Identify every addressable location and every street with a persistent number, so property and street data can be joined across organisations.
standards.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 (the identifiers and their grid references)
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: UPRN, Endorsed, updated 2020-12-16. GOV.UK's 'Identifying property and street information' (search-sourced) says systems that store or publish property and street data must use UPRN and USRN; open under OGL since July 2020.

standards.name: Digital Object Identifier (DOI) System
standards.publisher: International DOI Foundation (endorsed by the DSA)
standards.purpose: Persistent identifiers for research and information assets.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: Digital Object identifier System, Endorsed, tag Identification.

standards.name: ISO 20022 (universal financial industry message scheme)
standards.purpose: A common language for payment and financial messages.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: Universal financial industry message scheme, In review, updated 2021-02-02.

standards.name: Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus
standards.publisher: DSIT and NCSC, delivered by IASME
standards.purpose: A baseline of technical controls against the most common cyber attacks, with an audited Plus level.
standards.evidence: PPN 014 (updated February 2025, search-sourced): since 2014 suppliers bidding for certain public contracts must hold Cyber Essentials or Cyber Essentials Plus, or show equivalent controls; not to be applied to all contracts as a matter of course.

standards.name: GovAssure
standards.purpose: The scheme that assesses government's critical systems against the Baseline or Enhanced government CAF profile.
standards.evidence: security.gov.uk pages found by search on 20 November 2026: GovAssure is the cyber security assurance scheme for government's critical systems and uses the NCSC CAF.

standards.name: NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)
standards.purpose: Assess how well an organisation meets cyber security and resilience outcomes, against a CAF profile.
standards.evidence: NCSC CAF collection page (search-sourced, 20 November 2026). Government CAF profiles (Baseline and Enhanced) are used by GovAssure; GovAssure used CAF 3.2 for 2025-26 assessments (security.gov.uk, search-sourced).

standards.name: Secure by Design
standards.appliesTo: Central government and arm's length bodies; optional for the wider public sector
standards.publisher: Government Security Group, DSIT and NCSC
standards.purpose: Build cyber security into digital services from the start and through their life: 10 principles and supporting activities.
standards.evidence: security.gov.uk pages found by search on 20 November 2026: the policy applies to central government organisations and ALBs and may be optionally adopted by other parts of the public sector; meeting the 10 principles is mandatory for services under the digital and technology spend control.

standards.name: security.txt (RFC 9116)
standards.purpose: A file at a well-known address telling people how to report a security vulnerability.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: Security.txt, Endorsed, tags Vulnerability, Reporting, Security.

standards.name: Cyber Governance Code of Practice
standards.purpose: The governance actions boards and directors should take on cyber risk.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK page found by search on 20 November 2026: published 8 April 2025. DSIT says all organisations relying on digital services should aim to implement it and hold Cyber Essentials.

standards.name: Software Security Code of Practice
standards.appliesTo: Organisations that develop or sell software to other organisations
standards.purpose: 14 principles for software vendors to reduce supply chain attacks and resilience failures.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK page found by search on 20 November 2026: launched 7 May 2025, last updated 15 January 2026; voluntary.

standards.name: Government Functional Standard GovS 005: Digital
standards.purpose: Sets expectations for managing digital and data across government organisations.
standards.evidence: Version 2.2 (2026) found by search on 20 November 2026: replaces 2.1 and broadens the scope to government digital and data.

standards.name: Service Standard
standards.appliesTo: UK government services (assessed for in-scope services)
standards.purpose: The 14 points government services must meet, from understanding users to making the service accessible and secure.
standards.evidence: Referred to by the Technology Code of Practice page (search-sourced, 20 November 2026). Link and summary from background knowledge; page not re-read this session.

standards.name: Technology Code of Practice
standards.purpose: Criteria for how government designs, builds and buys technology, including using open standards and making better use of data.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK pages found by search on 20 November 2026: align with the mandatory points and follow as many of the rest as practical; point 10 is 'Make better use of data'.

standards.name: WCAG 2.2 level AA and the public sector accessibility regulations
standards.appliesTo: UK public sector websites and apps
standards.publisher: W3C; required by the Public Sector Bodies Accessibility Regulations 2018
standards.purpose: The accessibility level public sector websites and apps must meet, with an accessibility statement.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK pages found by search on 20 November 2026: services must meet WCAG 2.2 AA as a minimum and publish an accessibility statement; monitoring against WCAG 2.2 AA began from October 2024 (accessibility blog).

standards.name: Digital Scotland Service Standard
standards.appliesTo: Organisations delivering public services in Scotland
standards.purpose: 14 criteria for public services in Scotland, built on the GDS Service Standard.
standards.status: All organisations asked to work towards it
standards.evidence: Scottish Government digital blog (search-sourced, 20 November 2026): replaced the Digital First Service Standard, reducing 22 criteria to 14; all organisations are asked to work towards it.

standards.name: Digital Service Standard for Wales
standards.purpose: Principles to help everyone in Wales provide better services.
standards.evidence: GOV.WALES page found by search on 20 November 2026: first published 11 March 2022.

standards.name: GPG 45: How to check someone's identity
standards.appliesTo: Anyone checking identity, including GOV.UK One Login
standards.publisher: Office for Digital Identities and Attributes (DSIT)
standards.purpose: A method for checking identity to a chosen level of confidence.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK page found by search on 20 November 2026: the 1.0 pre-release accompanies the 1.0 trust framework. The Digital Economy Act register's agreement 353 says identities must meet GPG 45 Medium for HMRC services through GOV.UK One Login.

standards.name: UK digital verification services trust framework
standards.publisher: Office for Digital Identities and Attributes (DSIT)
standards.purpose: Government-backed rules for trustworthy digital identity services, with independent certification.
standards.evidence: GOV.UK pages found by search on 20 November 2026: organisations can choose to be independently certified against the trust framework; it builds on GPG 45.

standards.name: FHIR UK Core (HL7 FHIR R4)
standards.appliesTo: Health and care IT in England (NHS service standard)
standards.purpose: The UK profile of HL7 FHIR for health and care APIs.
standards.evidence: NHS standards directory (DAPB4020, active) and NHS service standard point 17 (search-sourced, 20 November 2026): use FHIR UK Core when building new APIs.

standards.name: NHS number
standards.appliesTo: Identifying patients in England, Wales and the Isle of Man
standards.purpose: The patient identifier used across health and care records and APIs.
standards.evidence: NHS service standard point 17 (search-sourced, 20 November 2026): where appropriate, use the NHS number to identify patients on APIs. The Digital Economy Act register's agreement 79 shares NHS numbers linked with birth and death registrations.

standards.name: SNOMED CT
standards.purpose: The structured clinical vocabulary for electronic care records.
standards.evidence: NHS service standard point 17 (search-sourced, 20 November 2026): use SNOMED CT for electronic care records.

standards.name: Open Contracting Data Standard (OCDS)
standards.publisher: Open Contracting Partnership; used by the Cabinet Office central digital platform
standards.purpose: Publish procurement data in one structured format across the whole procurement process.
standards.status: Selected by the Open Standards Board; used for all notices under the Procurement Act 2023
standards.evidence: Selected for use across government by the Open Standards Board (government technology blog, search-sourced). GOV.UK guidance on the Procurement Act 2023 central digital platform (updated 17 August 2026, search-sourced) says it publishes information in line with OCDS throughout the procurement process.

standards.name: Algorithmic Transparency Reporting Standard (ATRS)
standards.purpose: A standard way for public sector bodies to publish information about the algorithmic tools they use.
standards.evidence: Read at the DSA Standards Catalogue page (published 28 July 2023, updated 25 October 2023) on 8 November 2026: listed as Endorsed, OGL. The catalogue names it the Reporting Standard; GOV.UK pages also use Recording Standard.

standards.name: Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS) v0.3
standards.purpose: Collect, use, exchange and publish information about who owns and controls companies and other legal entities.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: "Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS) v0.3", Endorsed, updated 2022-03-16. The earlier reading (8 November 2026) of the GOV.UK catalogue page found its heading said v0.3 and its text v0.2; the DSA list settles it as v0.3.

standards.name: International Aid Transparency Initiative (IATI) Standard
standards.purpose: Publish information about aid and development spending in one format.
standards.evidence: Selected for use across government by the Open Standards Board, alongside OCDS (government technology blog, search-sourced, 20 November 2026).

standards.name: 360Giving Data Standard
standards.purpose: Publish grants data in one format so funders' grants can be compared.
standards.evidence: Read at the Data Standards Authority list (alphagov.github.io/data-standards-authority/standards) on 20 November 2026: 360Giving Schema, In review, updated 2021-02-02.
